# Github logo should be the official one

## Problem statement

The main menu's GitHub footer link renders a generic octopus emoji (`🐙`) as its
icon. This is not the official GitHub logo, so the menu does not present an
accurate brand mark for the repository link.

## Users

- **Player/Visitor:** Sees the menu and recognises the GitHub link by its
  familiar brand mark.
- **Contributor/Maintainer:** Wants the shipped game to display the official
  GitHub branding rather than a placeholder emoji.

### User stories

- *As a player, I see the official GitHub logo next to the "GitHub" text on the
  main menu, so I can recognise the repository link at a glance.*
- *As a maintainer, I know the footer link uses the correct GitHub brand asset,
  not a stand-in emoji, so the game presents professional branding.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Official logo rendered:** The `MenuScene` footer GitHub link renders
   the official GitHub logo (Octocat mark) as an image asset, replacing the
   current `🐙` emoji icon.
2. **AC2 — Label retained:** The "GitHub" text label remains next to the logo
   (icon + text layout), preserving the existing label-based discoverability.
3. **AC3 — Behaviour unchanged:** The link keeps its current position
   (bottom-left), interactivity (pointer + keyboard via `FocusManager`), hover
   colour, and click target (`GITHUB_REPO_URL`, new tab via
   `noopener,noreferrer`). Tab order is unchanged.
4. **AC4 — Tests:** Unit tests in `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` verify the
   official logo asset renders alongside the "GitHub" label and that the link
   still opens `GITHUB_REPO_URL` on activation. Any existing assertions that
   match the `🐙` emoji are updated.
5. **AC5 — Docs & suite:** Code comments are updated to reflect the change; the
   full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Code-first convention (GDD §6.3):** The game is built primarily through
  code; art assets are kept minimal. The logo is a small, single-purpose
  vendored brand asset — an acceptable one-time exception approved by the
  operator (Q1 answer A).
- **No keyboard regression:** The Tab cycle (Play → Demo → Settings →
  Leaderboard → GitHub → Gym) must remain unchanged. `FocusManager` registration
  keys on a text label, so the control must keep a text label (or the registry
  entry must be updated consistently).
- **No layout regression:** The GitHub link stays at `(16, GAME_HEIGHT − 12)`
  with `setOrigin(0, 1)`, so the future version-number label beneath it
  (AH-0MUZM9053008YXOZ) remains compatible.
- **Official source:** The asset must be the official GitHub Octocat mark from
  GitHub's brand/download resources (e.g. `github-mark` SVG/PNG), not a
  third-party re-draw.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` renders `GITHUB_LINK_LABEL = '🐙  GitHub'` as a
  single Phaser text object, positioned at `(16, GAME_HEIGHT − 12)` with
  `setOrigin(0, 1)`, registered with `FocusManager` (AH-0MUZI83EO003WVTG).
- `GITHUB_REPO_URL` is a single source of truth in `src/core/constants.ts`.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` matches the `🐙  GitHub` label in multiple
  assertions (render, pointer, keyboard, tab order) via a `findText` helper.
- The project has no existing runtime image assets loaded via
  `this.load.image`/`preload`; audio is baked via ToneForge. `public/` contains
  only `audio/`.

## Desired change

- Add a container in `MenuScene` for the GitHub link that combines the official
  GitHub logo image (loaded via Phaser's image loader from a vendored asset)
  and the existing "GitHub" text label.
- Add a `preload()` (or lazy image load) in `MenuScene` for the logo asset, and
  vendor the asset under `public/` (e.g. `public/images/github-mark.svg` or a
  PNG equivalent) so it is served by the build.
- Keep the combined hit area interactive and registered with `FocusManager`,
  with the existing pointer and keyboard handlers.
- Update tests to locate the GitHub link by label text and/or the rendered
  logo image.

## Implementation notes

- Add a `preload()` lifecycle method (or lazy `this.load.image` call) to
  `MenuScene` for the vendored logo asset, then build a `Phaser.GameObjects.Container`
  with the logo image + text label, or position them at the same anchor point
  with the same hit area.
- Keep `GITHUB_LINK_LABEL` (or an equivalent label constant) so `FocusManager`
  tab-order tests keep passing with minimal churn; update tests to assert the
  logo image object exists (e.g. via `scene.children` scan) in addition to the
  label.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — Render the official logo + label; add preload for the asset.
- `public/images/github-mark.*` (new) — Vendored official GitHub Octocat mark asset.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` — Update `🐙` assertions; add a test for the rendered logo.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — Possibly document the new asset path if referenced there.

## Related work

- **Add a GitHub link to the main menu** (AH-0MUZI83EO003WVTG) — parent work
  item that introduced the footer link and the `🐙` label.
- **Add version number to the menu screen** (AH-0MUZM9053008YXOZ) — sibling;
  places a version label beneath the GitHub link; position must remain
  compatible with this change.
- **Create Main Menu scene** (AH-0MU72YVFR005VB2N) — parent menu work.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B** – Bullets from the players ship should always fall on the beat (completed) — keyword match only; not related to this change.
- **AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR** – Test: P10 parity across PlayScene, GymMinerals and GymPowerUpsUtility (completed) — keyword match only; not related.
- **AH-0MUPP1Q7S009NFHE** – The default weapon pickup should not reset weapons (completed) — keyword match only; not related.

### Repository file matches
- `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched on generic keywords (github/icon/menu); no logo/branding content in these files.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Asset accuracy:** The vendored mark must be GitHub's official Octocat SVG to
  satisfy "official logo"; a stylised re-draw would not. Assumption: operator
  accepts an external brand asset (Q1 A).
- **Image-loading timing:** Phaser image loads are async; the link must not
  render the logo half-loaded or fail silently in tests (handle load event in
  `preload()`).
- **Font/emoji fallback:** Replacing the emoji removes cross-platform emoji
  rendering variance, which is a side benefit.
- **Scope creep:** Updating the logo in other scenes (gym index, docs, README
  favicon) is explicitly out of scope for this item (Q3 A); could be follow-up
  work if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q (Round 1): "What form should the 'official GitHub logo' take in the game?"
  — Answer (operator): "A — Vendored Octocat mark (SVG/PNG) loaded as a Phaser
  asset." Source: interactive reply. Research: project has no runtime image
  assets today (public/audio only); Phaser `load.image`/`load.svg` supports a
  small budget. Accepted: code-first exception for a single brand asset.
- Q (Round 1): "Should the label text remain next to the logo?" — Answer
  (operator): "A — Keep the 'GitHub' text label." Source: interactive reply.
- Q (Round 1): "Scope — menu only or elsewhere?" — Answer (operator): "A — Main
  menu (MenuScene) only." Source: interactive reply. Accepted; other locations
  (gym index, favicon) are out of scope (scope-creep note added).

# Cluster missile split fan is mis-phased (warhead flies 180° backwards)

## Problem statement

At its base ("Lvl 1") level a cluster missile fans its two warheads with a
**0° phase**: one warhead continues straight along the parent missile's heading
(so it reads as "no split") and the other flies exactly **180° backwards** — the
opposite of the intended MIRV cluster. The weapon therefore looks like a single
missile travelling away from the direction of fire, and the split does not
cover the space around the projectile as designed.

## Users

As a **player**, I want a cluster missile to burst into warheads spread
**around** the direction of travel — starting at **90° and 270°** at base level
— so that a single shot covers a group of enemies instead of sending a warhead
uselessly backwards. As the weapon levels up, the extra warheads should
continue to **divide the full 360° circle evenly**.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` `splitProjectile()` computes
  `angle = baseHeading + (2 * Math.PI * i) / count`. At `count = 2` the warheads
  are `0°` and `180°` relative to the parent heading.
- `WEAPON_CATALOGUE.cluster.splits = CLUSTER_BASE_WARHEADS = 2`
  (`src/utils/weapons.ts`).
- `resolveWeaponDefinition('cluster', level)` grows `splits` with the
  `splitCount` variable, currently clamped so the **total** warhead count never
  exceeds the spec cap of `3` (`src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`).
- The player's resolver level is `weaponLevel − 1`: the first collection is the
  base stats (`src/entities/Player.ts` `_weaponUpgradeIndex`).
- The split is a single shared seam consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym;
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` asserts identical warhead
  velocities in the game and `GymWeapons`.

## Desired change

- Phase the radial fan at **+90°** so the first warhead is perpendicular to the
  parent heading: `angle = baseHeading + Math.PI / 2 + (2 * Math.PI * i) / count`.
- Base count `2` → headings `90°` and `270°` relative to the parent heading.
  Count `3` → `90°`, `210°`, `330°`. Count `N` → evenly spaced `360°/N`,
  always phase-locked to the parent heading so the burst stays predictable.
- Keep the existing single shared `splitProjectile` implementation (game + gyms)
  and all other cluster tuning (cadence, colour, lifetime, warhead speed).

## Acceptance Criteria

- At the base cluster level (`resolveWeaponDefinition('cluster', 0)`, i.e. the
  first collection) a fired missile splits into **at least two** warheads —
  verified by a unit test.
- With exactly two warheads their headings are offset by **+90°** and **−90°**
  (i.e. 90° and 270°) from the parent missile's heading, and neither warhead
  travels at 0° or 180° — verified by a deterministic unit test (e.g. a missile
  fired to the right).
- For any warhead count `n` the warheads are **evenly spaced `2π/n` apart**
  around the parent heading with a constant `+90°` phase offset — verified by a
  unit test for at least `n = 2` and `n = 3`.
- Each warhead keeps the parent missile's speed and remains an ordinary
  `PlayerBullet` that damages enemies on contact through the shared collision
  path (the split-burst VFX is unchanged) — verified by a unit test.
- The split resolves **exactly once** per projectile (on first impact or
  expiry) and the parent shell is consumed — verified by a unit test.
- Warhead count continues to grow **monotonically** with weapon level through
  `resolveWeaponDefinition` within the existing `splitCount` spec cap — verified
  by a unit test (existing behaviour preserved).
- Gym↔game parity is preserved: the fan is produced only by the shared
  `splitProjectile` seam in `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`, and the
  existing game + `GymWeapons` parity test stays green — verified by
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the **single shared implementation** in `src/scenes/core/`; do not add
  per-scene copies (repo gym↔game parity rule).
- Do **not** change the cluster fire cadence (0.5 subdivision / 1500 ms at
  80 BPM), colour, lifetime, or the base warhead count of 2.
- Stay within the existing `splitCount` spec cap (3 total warheads) unless a
  separate balance decision changes it (recorded as an assumption below).
- Warheads remain ordinary `PlayerBullet`s — no new entity types and no
  `AoEDescriptor`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `splitProjectile()`: add the `+π/2`
  fan phase offset (and update the doc comment).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts` — cluster split-seam tests: assert the
  perpendicular base headings and even `360°/n` spacing.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — existing game/`GymWeapons`
  parity test already compares warhead velocities; extend with a phase
  assertion if practical.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — clarify the `CLUSTER_BASE_WARHEADS` / `cluster`
  comments to describe the perpendicular base fan.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — document the warhead-count cap semantics if the
  assumption is confirmed.
- `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` — describe the 90°/270° base fan and
  the even division of the 360° circle at higher levels.

## Related work

- **Missile Command cluster/MIRV missile (AH-0MV1BIVIJ007KYXU)** — the completed
  feature that introduced the split seam and this fan-phase behaviour; this bug
  fixes it.
- **New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4)** —
  parent epic.
- `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` — design brief for the cluster
  missile.

## Assumptions

- **"Lvl 1" = the weapon's base (first-collection) level.** `_weaponUpgradeIndex`
  makes the first collection resolver level 0, where `splits = 2` at headings
  0°/180° — matching the report of "a single missile travelling 180° backwards".
  If "Lvl 1" instead means a later upgrade, the base-count AC still holds and
  the phase fix still applies.
- **The warhead-count cap is unchanged** for this bug fix. The `splitCount`
  spec describes *extra* fragments (cap 3) while `resolveWeaponDefinition`
  clamps the *total* count to 3; interpreting the report's "further divide the
  360° circle" as satisfied by even spacing rather than by raising the cap keeps
  this change scoped to the reported defect. Raising the cap is a separate
  balance decision.
- The cluster remains a **timed** weapon drop (drop round-robin and HUD rows
  unchanged).
- **Scope-creep guard:** extra opportunities discovered while fixing (e.g. raising
  the warhead cap, re-balancing the split damage, re-tuning the burst VFX) are
  recorded as linked work items — **not** folded into this bug fix.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Does 'Lvl1' mean the weapon's base/first-collection level, or the game's
  first stage at some weapon upgrade?" — Answer: **assumed base/first-collection
  level** (resolver level 0), where `_weaponUpgradeIndex = weaponLevel − 1`
  gives `splits = 2` at headings 0°/180°, matching the reported "single missile
  travelling 180°". Source: `src/entities/Player.ts` `_weaponUpgradeIndex`,
  `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` `resolveWeaponDefinition`. Producer confirmation
  welcome; the fix is unaffected either way.
- Q: "Should later levels add more warheads than the current cap of 3 total?" —
  Answer: **assumed out of scope**; the existing `splitCount` cap semantics are
  preserved and only the fan phase changes. Source: `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`
  and `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md`. If the producer wants more
  warheads at later levels, that is a separate balance change.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU7JTFM5000R4ME** – Power-ups spawn too close together (completed)
- **AH-0MUD9R3NB0093CBV** – Extract player-hit lifecycle into CombatScene (completed)
- **AH-0MUD9R2C5000FY60** – Define CombatScene hook contract with stub-subclass tests (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mv14so0g0095ij4, 0mv1bivij007kyxu, add, along, already (+254 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mv14so0g0095ij4, 0mv1bivij007kyxu, acceptance, add, along (+246 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mv14so0g0095ij4, add, along, already, always (+210 more)
